children: EPRA earnings per share increased to 8.1p from 7.3p, while net rental income rose 5.3% to £130.2m. The company also increased its total dividend by 3% to 8.56p per share, extending its track record of annual dividend growth.

The results reinforced the strength of the group's operating platform at a time when many real estate companies continue to grapple with the effects of higher interest rates. Occupancy remained at 97%, while like-for-like rental growth came in at 3.2%, reflecting the favourable supply-demand dynamics that continue to underpin the UK rental market.

Despite the strong operational performance, Grainger reported a statutory pre-tax loss of £41.8 million, compared with a profit of £102.6m a year earlier. The swing was driven primarily by £116m of property valuation losses as higher financing costs continued to weigh on real estate asset values across the sector. As a result, EPRA net tangible assets fell 6% to 281p per share.

Management used the results to highlight the next stage of the company's development. After spending much of the past decade building one of the UK's largest build-to-rent platforms, Grainger is now approaching the end of a major investment cycle.
Only £87m of committed development expenditure remains, leaving the company increasingly focused on extracting value from completed assets rather than funding significant new projects.

Balance sheet management is expected to become a key theme over the coming years. The company has identified approximately £825m of lower-return and non-core assets for disposal, with proceeds earmarked for debt reduction and capital recycling. Grainger completed £147m of disposals during the year and entered the new financial year with a further £40m of sales in progress.

Net debt stood at £1.49bn at the year-end, while loan-to-value increased to 40.7% from 38.4%, largely reflecting lower asset valuations rather than increased borrowing. Nevertheless, the group's average cost of debt remained relatively low at 3.2%, providing some insulation from higher interest rates.

Management reiterated its target of increasing EPRA earnings to Â£72 million, or 9.7p per share, by FY29, implying growth of around 20% from current levels. Much of that increase is expected to come from recently completed developments reaching maturity and from the benefits of lower leverage as disposal proceeds are reinvested in the balance sheet.

Grainger said the outlook remains underpinned by structural drivers that continue to favour the rented residential sector. Chronic housing shortages, affordability challenges facing prospective homeowners and growing demand for institutionally managed accommodation should support rental growth and occupancy levels.
Reporting by Frank Prenesti for Sharecast.com
